hook.text: Stretch the silicon lattice slightly and electrons speed up — strain makes transistors faster for free.

buildup.text: Embedding silicon-germanium under the channel compresses it — changing the band structure to boost mobility.

discovery.text: Intel added strain at 90 nm and saw a 25% speed boost — no shrinking required.

twist.text: Too much strain creates dislocations — cracks in the crystal that kill transistor reliability.

climax.text: Every advanced node since 2003 uses strain — it is the silent partner behind every performance jump.

punchline.text: Stretch the crystal and electrons move faster — free speed.

quiz.question: How does strain engineering improve transistor speed?
options: It heats the channel to increase electron energy
Stretching the lattice changes the band structure, boosting electron mobility
It adds more dopant atoms to the channel
